office.name: Otero County Sheriff's Office
office.place: Otero County, Colorado; administration building and detention center at 222 E. 2nd St., La Junta, CO 81050 (opened 2025)
office.main_phone: (719) 384-5941 (main line; used in replies for general questions)
office.remit: An elected county constitutional officer. The sheriff runs the county jail (detention center), patrols the unincorporated county, serves civil process and executes court orders, provides courthouse security, issues concealed handgun permits, and is the county fire warden for prairie and wildland fires outside fire district capability (C.R.S. 30-10-513). In Otero County the Office of Emergency Management is a division of the Sheriff's Office and runs the county's opt-in emergency alert system. The sheriff hires and directs staff, but the office is funded from the county general fund through a budget the Board of County Commissioners adopts each December, and contracts are approved and signed by the Board (the sheriff is not a body corporate). The Board holds public hearings on the 2nd and 4th Mondays.

official.background: Age 58. Grew up in Manzanola. Twenty-six years with the Colorado State Patrol, retired in 2025 as a sergeant at the La Junta troop office. Former Manzanola volunteer firefighter. First county office. Pledged when appointed not to seek election in November; serves until the sheriff-elect is sworn in.

succession.rule: Colorado Constitution, Article XIV, Section 9: in case of a vacancy in any county office other than county commissioner, the board of county commissioners fills it by appointment, and the appointee holds office until the next general election or until the vacancy is filled by election. C.R.S. 30-10-505: when the office of sheriff is vacant, the undersheriff executes the office until a sheriff is appointed or elected and qualified. County officers' terms begin the second Tuesday of January after their election (Colorado Constitution, Article XIV, Section 8), so the person elected on November 3, 2026 takes office Tuesday, January 12, 2027.
succession.timeline: Fri Sept 4, 2026: previous sheriff's retirement effective; Undersheriff Dana Kroeker acting sheriff under C.R.S. 30-10-505. Mon Sept 14: Board of County Commissioners public hearing adopts Resolution 2026-58 appointing Lonnie Strohm (letters of support and public comment taken). Tue Sept 15: oath administered by the county clerk, Otero County Courthouse, La Junta; Strohm takes office.
succession.ballot: The sheriff's office is on the regular November 3, 2026 ballot (four-year term starting January 12, 2027). The previous sheriff's retirement and the November race are never discussed in the drive; candidates are never named. Strohm told the Board he would not be a candidate, which is why he was chosen as a caretaker appointee.
